question.problem:
$\qquad$ $x$ is prime and $y$ divides $12$.

What is the negation of the composite predicate above?
question.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for conjunctions states that

$$
\neg ( A \land B) = \neg A \lor \neg B.
$$

So, the negation of "$x$ is prime and $y$ divides $12$" is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(x\text{ is prime and }y\text{ divides }12) & ≡¬(x\text{ is prime}∧y\text{ divides }12) \\  & ≡¬(x\text{ is prime})∨¬(y\text{ divides }12) \\  & ≡x\text{ is not prime}∨y\text{ does not divide }12 \\  & ≡x\text{ is not prime}\text{ or }y\text{ does not divide }12.\end{aligned}
$$
